problem.p: External clients read some documents at fixed paths of a site, before they access anything else. Examples: /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116), /robots.txt (RFC 9309), /.well-known/apple-app-site-association (iOS universal links), /.well-known/assetlinks.json (Android app links), /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/<resource> (RFC 9728).

In kajenn an application answers a /.well-known/ document only as a child of a reserved _well_known branch of its router, built in code before the server registers it. A mixin cannot bring its own documents into an application, a fixed path outside /.well-known/ such as /robots.txt has no mechanism, and two applications declaring the same name are resolved silently by registration order.
genropy legacy answers these documents with webtools that declare their public path on the class (alias_url). This proposal brings that model to kajenn applications.

section.title: kajenn today
section.fact: A first path segment starting with a dot gets 404 from the server demux. The one exception is .well-known followed by a name in well_known_applications: the request goes to that application with its path rewritten as /_well_known/<name>/<rest>.
A RoutedApplication declares its documents as the children of a _well_known branch of its router. well_known_names returns those children.
register_application sets app.server = self, then indexes app.well_known_names once. A name declared by two applications belongs to the last registered. A claimed code or mount raises ValueError.
An external application presents its names in meta["well_known"], a list of strings, when its process joins the KajennBus.
A path without a leading dot, /robots.txt and /favicon.ico included, is demuxed like any other path: the root application if there is one, else 404.
SiteHome.static names a folder for the site's static files. No code serves it.
BaseApplication.__init__ receives code and mount from the recipe and sets self.mount. The class does not know its mount.
Each application has one class attribute grammar, inherited by MRO and mounted in the recipe under its application(app_class=...) element. Composition is explicit; a mixin cannot add words.
genro-builders 0.30.0 composes the elements of plain mixin bases of a grammar class: elements with different names are united; an element with the same name is replaced entirely.

section.title: genropy legacy
section.fact: At startup the site reads alias_url from every webtool and builds webtools_static_routes, a dict absolute path → webtool. _dispatcher looks the exact path up before every other rule.
DeepLinkIOS always associates the whole site ("/": "/*"); the configuration only excludes paths. It also emits webcredentials with the same app ids.
DeepLinkAndroid emits package name, certificate fingerprints and the relations handle_all_urls and get_login_creds. It has no paths.

list.item: An application class or a mixin declares the well-known URLs it answers in a class dict well_known: public path → route path inside the application.

What is well-known is fixed by the standards, not configured: /.well-known/... (RFC 8615), /robots.txt (RFC 9309), /favicon.ico (the HTML default icon). RFC 8615 cites /robots.txt and /favicon.ico as the site-wide metadata that predates the prefix.

A request whose path is well-known goes to the declared route of the declaring application. A well-known path nobody declared answers 404 with the message "unimplemented well-known URL": for robots.txt a 4xx means "no restrictions" (RFC 9309), for the other documents "not supported".
Two applications declaring the same path stop the server at construction. Inside one application the more derived class wins.
A path that depends on the mount (OAuth protected resources) is declared once on the class with the marker {mount}.
The site author is responsible for what a well-known route answers: kajenn does not check that it is public.

section.title: Declaring well-known URLs

list.item: Keys are public paths with the leading /. Values are route paths inside the application, without it.

BaseApplication.__init__ merges the dicts along the MRO (the more derived class wins on the same key), replaces {mount} with self.mount and stores the result in self.well_known. For the root mount ("") the segment /{mount} is removed whole: RFC 9728 has no trailing slash for a root resource.
A key that is not a well-known path is a construction error.
An application mounted twice gets one key per mount for {mount} keys; a key without the marker declared by both instances is a conflict, which is correct: a site has one of each.
The well-known paths are one kajenn constant: ^/(\.well-known/.+|robots\.txt|favicon\.ico)$. It is not configurable. sitemap.xml is not in it: the sitemap protocol does not fix its location.

register_application reads app.well_known, checks that each route exists and builds one index public path → (application, route). A path already held by another application raises ValueError, like a claimed code or mount.

The demux matches the constant first. A declared path is forwarded to its application as the route path; an undeclared one answers 404 "unimplemented well-known URL". Other first segments starting with a dot stay 404.
The _well_known branch, WELL_KNOWN_ROOT, well_known_names and the rewrite in demux_hidden are removed.
An external application sends its well_known dict when it joins. A path held by another application refuses the join with kbus.Refused; its own re-join replaces its paths.
/.well-known/security.txt and /robots.txt are generated from words of ServerApplicationGrammar. robots.txt rules are validated at boot.
/favicon.ico is served as a file from home:/static.

_server registers each path only when its words are configured or its file exists. An application may answer any of them itself, for example a favicon per host; if both do, the server stops with the conflict error.
A mixin inside kajenn gives an application its mobile capability: its own grammar words, a routing class under mobile and the two keys of its well_known.
The recipe holds only real parameters: ios(team_id, bundle_id, paths, excluded_paths) and android(package_name, fingerprints, paths, excluded_paths). The routes build the fixed JSON.
iOS: paths is required, at least one, in Apple components syntax (*, ?), copied as is; exclusions are written first. No /* default.

Android: paths and excluded_paths are optional, same syntax, written as relation_extensions → dynamic_app_link_components (Dynamic App Links, Android 15 and later; older devices use the app manifest).
webcredentials (iOS) and get_login_creds (Android) are always emitted from the same identifiers. The app activates them on its side.
A platform without configuration registers no key. A mixin with no platform configured logs a warning at boot.

section.title: Grammar composition
section.p: BaseApplication.__init_subclass__ composes cls.grammar from the grammars declared along the MRO, so a mixin brings its words into every application that uses it. Only new elements are composed: an element with the same name replaces the earlier one, as genro-builders does today.

decision.question: How does an application say which well-known URLs it answers?

option.title: Children of a _well_known branch, as today
A route plugin carrying the public name
Pairs public path → route written in the recipe
A class dict well_known: public path → route

decision.choice: The application already knows the pairing; the recipe keeps only real parameters. It is the legacy alias_url model and needs no reserved branch.

decision.question: Which paths are well-known?

option.title: Only /.well-known/...
A regex the recipe can change
A kajenn constant with the locations fixed by standards

decision.choice: The regex is the standards: /.well-known/, robots.txt and favicon.ico. Nothing to configure.

decision.question: What answers a well-known path no application declared?

option.title: 404 with the message unimplemented well-known URL
The normal demux, so a root application still receives it

decision.choice: 404 is the standard answer for an absent document.

decision.question: What happens when two applications declare the same path?

option.title: ValueError at construction; an external join is refused
The last registered wins, as today
An override flag lets one declaration replace the other

decision.choice: No silent winner. The override flag was discussed and not adopted: with _server declaring only what is configured no case needs it, and two overrides would conflict again.

decision.question: How is a path that contains the mount declared?

option.title: Added on the instance in __init__
Forbid two instances of one class
Regex keys
A {mount} marker in the class key

decision.choice: The declaration stays on the class. Forbidding two instances does not help, because the recipe chooses the mount anyway; regex keys are ambiguous between applications and their overlap cannot be checked at construction.

decision.question: Does kajenn check that a well-known route is public?

option.title: Yes, at registration
No

decision.choice: The site author knows what the route answers.

decision.question: How are /robots.txt and /favicon.ico available without writing an application?

option.title: Both as files from home:/static
Not at all: an application declares them
robots.txt from _server words, favicon.ico from home:/static

decision.choice: robots.txt has rules worth validating at boot; favicon.ico is an image.

decision.question: Which site paths does the mobile app open?

option.title: iOS paths required; Android paths optional
The whole site (/*), as legacy

decision.choice: Apple does not require /*, and its documentation uses specific paths. Android paths serve Dynamic App Links; the Android app is being prepared.

decision.question: What happens when an application has the mobile mixin and the recipe configures no platform?

option.title: Construction fails
Each platform registers only if configured; a warning when none is

decision.choice: Platforms are independent: iOS can be ready before Android.

decision.question: Where does the mobile mixin live?

option.title: Inside kajenn
A separate package

decision.question: Can a class extend an element of an inherited grammar instead of replacing it?

option.title: Yes, with @element(..., extend=True) in genro-builders
Not now: only new elements are composed

decision.choice: The mobile mixin needs only new words. extend=True is the chosen form when a case needs it.

list.item: The _well_known branch, WELL_KNOWN_ROOT and well_known_names are removed: a breaking change, released as a minor version.
The proposal channels-meta-and-server-gui no longer needs a _meta/well_known branch.
A site whose root application answers /favicon.ico today must declare it in that application's well_known.

The guide docs/guides/hidden-paths.md is rewritten with one table: for each case, who answers, when construction stops, when the answer is 404 "unimplemented well-known URL". The {mount} marker and the MRO merge are documented with examples.

Tests on the kajenn router cannot prove what an external client sees. A deployment check requests each declared document on the public HTTPS address, through the proxy, and fails on any status other than 200, on a redirect or on a body that does not parse.
